title: An Autonomous, Preregistered Evaluation of a Deterministic Provenance‑Scoring Judge for LLM NetOps "No‑Issue" Assertions
abstract: We evaluate whether a deterministic provenance+validator judge (retrieval grounding, syntactic/semantic validators, telemetry cross‑checks) reduces unsupported LLM "no‑issue" (reachability/health‑holds) assertions in scripted NetOps emulator scenarios. Following a machine‑readable preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1) we ran a paired confirmatory execution with gpt-5-mini across 90 seeded tasks (planned 180 episodes). Execution completed 166 episodes (14 failed) yielding 83 complete paired tasks. Baseline (LLM only) successes: 81/83 (97.59%); guarded (judge) successes: 83/83 (100.0%). Absolute paired improvement = 0.0240963855; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.000, 0.0602409639] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). McNemar two‑sided exact p = 0.50. The guarded pipeline changed two discordant pairs in this synthetic setting; the improvement is numerically small and statistically inconclusive given realized sample size. All execution artifacts, provider_call logs, and SHA256 hashes are recorded in the run manifest (execution/ in the artifact bundle) and are the authoritative reproducible record for this study. We report preregistration→analysis deviations, missingness accounting, and bounded operational conclusions limited to scripted/emulator scenarios.

sections.introduction: Generative models and agentic LLMs are being proposed for NetOps tasks (intent translation, diagnosis, limited self‑healing). A recurrent operational risk is a fluent LLM output asserting “no issue” or “reachability holds” without programmatic evidence; such unsupported assertions can mislead automation or operators. We asked: can a deterministic, programmatic provenance+validator judge reliably distinguish supported from unsupported LLM "no‑issue" assertions in scripted emulator NetOps scenarios? We contribute (1) a machine‑readable preregistration (cand-2026-003‑provenance‑prereg‑v1) freezing design and analysis choices; (2) an autonomous paired confirmatory execution with full artifact hashing; (3) a preregistered paired analysis and transparent accounting of deviations; and (4) an evidence‑bounded interpretation for emulator settings.
sections.related_work: Layered mitigation patterns (retrieval grounding, schema/validator checks, evidence scoring, tool‑augmented repair) and taxonomies of LLM epistemic failures motivate combining deterministic signals before operational acceptance. Prior NetOps/IBN studies emphasise assurance contracts, bounded tools, and canary/rollback practices rather than sole model reliance. Our work operationalises a generate→validate→gate pattern in a preregistered, emulator‑only experiment and publishes an execution manifest to support reproducibility and audit.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1) fixed research question, paired baseline/guarded design, task bank size (90 seeded emulator scenarios), episode budget (180), model (gpt-5-mini), seeds, retry/replacement policy, primary and secondary estimands, and analysis pipeline. Judge architecture (frozen) combined: (A) deterministic retrieval grounding (index snapshot), (B) syntactic/semantic validators for config/command consistency, and (C) telemetry cross‑checks against deterministic emulator state. Implementation and logging. Adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model: gpt-5-mini (hosted provider). All prompts, provider_call logs, model responses, and scoring JSONs were recorded; SHA256 hashes are enumerated in the execution manifest (execution/artifact_hashes). Episode handling. Up to two automatic deterministic retries for emulator or parser failures; if unresolved the preregistered deterministic replacement policy attempted to preserve the planned task_count. Scoring rules (frozen): each episode parsed to extract one canonical "no‑issue/reachability holds" assertion (when present) and deterministically labeled supported/unsupported by comparison to emulator ground truth. Analysis plan (applied). The preregistration specified F1 on a held‑out split as the primary estimand, but the completed run produced paired episodes with partial missingness; to preserve within‑task counterfactuals we applied the preregistered paired‑aware analysis machinery and report a paired contingency/McNemar analysis as our confirmatory inference (this analytic choice and its justification are declared in Deviations below). The preregistered secondary analyses and ablations (precision/recall with bootstrap CIs, calibration, signal ablations) remained planned but were not fully executed on the realized paired dataset (see Limitations).
sections.results: Execution accounting and provider audit. Planned: 90 tasks × 2 episodes = 180 episodes. Completed episodes: 166; failed episodes: 14 (handled per preregistered retry/replacement rules). Complete paired tasks available for confirmatory inference: 83 pairs. Provider/model calls: hosted_model_call_event_count = 92; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 7 (see execution/provider_calls/*.json in the manifest). Confirmatory paired counts (n=83): n_11 (both success) = 81; n_10 (guarded success only) = 2; n_01 (baseline success only) = 0; n_00 = 0. Baseline success rate = 81/83 = 0.9759036145. Guarded success rate = 83/83 = 1.0. Absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) = 0.0240963855. Paired bootstrap (percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% CI = [0.000, 0.060240963855421686]. McNemar exact two‑sided p = 0.50. The two discordant pairs favored the guarded condition: in those episodes the baseline LLM produced assertions the deterministic validators/telemetry marked unsupported while the guarded pipeline (which enforces evidence gates or triggers repair/clarification per the frozen judge logic) resulted in a supported outcome. All per‑episode scoring JSONs and provider_call logs are recorded and hashed in the execution manifest for audit.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. In this preregistered emulator run the guarded judge changed two baseline‑failed cases (absolute paired improvement ≈ 2.4 percentage points) but the paired bootstrap CI includes zero and McNemar p=0.50; with the realized paired n=83 the observed numerical change is small and not statistically conclusive. Operationally this provides bounded evidence that deterministic evidence‑gating can alter a small number of unsupported “no‑issue” outputs in scripted/emulator scenarios, but it does not establish production readiness or model‑family generality. Deviations and justification. The preregistered primary estimand was F1 on a held‑out split; in execution we obtained paired episodes with partial missingness (166/180 episodes completed) and therefore used the paired contingency/McNemar framework to preserve within‑task counterfactual comparability. This analytic change was made to honour the preregistered paired design and the deterministic missingness/replacement policy; the change and justification are declared here and the deterministic execution manifest records timing, replacement events, and retry attempts (see execution/execution_log.jsonl and deterministic_reconciliation). Provider‑call accounting. The realized model_calls_used (92) is below the naive episode budget because (i) some guarded episodes triggered deterministic short‑circuiting or local validator rejections before further provider calls (recorded in provider_call logs), and (ii) a small number of failed provider calls occurred and are recorded as failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 7. All provider_call JSONs and their SHA256 hashes are in the execution manifest. Threats to validity. Internal: prompt sensitivity and hosted provider nondeterminism; Construct: labels are emulator‑derived and may not capture production evidence modalities; External: single model (gpt-5-mini), scripted/emulator tasks; Conclusion validity: realized paired n=83 limits power for small absolute effects. Reproducibility. All raw responses, provider_call logs, scoring JSONs, seeds, and hashed artifacts are enumerated in the execution manifest (execution/artifact_hashes) and are the authoritative audit record for this run. The manifest lists file paths and SHA256 digests produced by the autonomous run; the run did not produce a single consolidated public repository URL within its artifacts and therefore no repository URL is being invented here (see Disclosure).
sections.conclusion: In this autonomous, preregistered execution over scripted NetOps emulator scenarios using gpt-5-mini, a deterministic provenance+validator judge produced a small numeric reduction in unsupported "no‑issue" assertions (2 discordant pairs out of 83 paired tasks). The paired bootstrap CI includes zero and McNemar p=0.50; thus the effect is numerically small and statistically inconclusive in this run. The finding supports a bounded claim: layered deterministic checks can change a small number of borderline cases in these synthetic settings. It does not establish production readiness, cross‑model generality, or broader NetOps external validity. Future work should enlarge the task bank and paired sample, run the preregistered ablations (retrieval vs telemetry vs validators), and evaluate multiple models and realistic telemetry/testbeds. All execution artifacts and hashes are published in the execution manifest to enable independent verification of the run outputs.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed under the CNSM 2026 Agentic AI Researcher requirements with an autonomy lock and a machine‑readable preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1). Human roles prior to the autonomy lock: the Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary and Master Prompt v1. After the lock the autonomous system performed literature review, final research selection, the machine‑readable preregistration, code generation, experiment orchestration, model calls, deterministic parsing/scoring, statistical analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. LLMs and orchestration: the hosted LLM used for the confirmatory execution was gpt-5-mini (model identifier recorded in execution/model_configuration.json); the orchestration/adapter family frozen in the preregistration was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt: the immutable Master Prompt v1 provided in the frozen input bundle (referenced in the overall project artifacts). Prompts, prompt templates, and judge logic (retrieval grounding + syntactic/semantic validators + telemetry cross‑checks) were frozen in the preregistration. Preregistration freeze: the preregistration fixed task bank size (90 seeded emulator scenarios), paired design, seeds, retry/replacement rules, maximum_model_calls (180), stopping rules, primary and secondary estimands, and the analysis plan. Execution artifacts and provenance: all raw LLM responses, provider_call logs, scoring JSONs, seeds, and per‑file SHA256 digests are recorded in the execution manifest (execution/artifact_hashes) produced by the autonomous run; the manifest paths and digests are the authoritative artifact record. The autonomous run did not produce a single consolidated public repository URL among its artifacts; consequently no repository URL is provided here. Technical restarts and deviations: the run followed the preregistered deterministic retry policy (up to two automatic retries for emulator or parser failures) and replacement policy; 14 episodes failed after retries and the completed episode count was 166 (complete paired tasks = 83). Model call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 92; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 7 (details in execution/provider_calls/*.json). No human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Limitations declared: experiments used synthetic/emulator scenarios only; single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) limits model generality; realized paired n=83 reduces statistical power; preregistered secondary analyses and ablations were not fully executed on the realized dataset and remain unresolved in this run (see Limitations). The Research Director reviewed and approved the design before the autonomy lock; all subsequent scientific decisions, execution steps, analyses, and manuscript text were produced autonomously and logged in the autonomous revision and execution records.
limitations: Evaluation limited to scripted synthetic/emulator scenarios; external validity to production NetOps environments is untested.
Single‑model experiment (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or versions.
Planned episodes (180) were not fully completed: 166 episodes completed, 14 failed after preregistered retries; complete paired tasks = 83, reducing confirmatory power for small effects.

Primary estimand divergence: preregistered primary estimand was F1 on a held‑out split; realized execution produced paired episodes and the confirmatory analysis used a paired contingency/McNemar framework to preserve within‑task counterfactuals — this analytic change is declared and justified in the manuscript but represents a deviation from the original estimand.

Preregistered secondary metrics and ablations (precision/recall with bootstrap CIs, Brier/calibration, retrieval/telemetry/validator ablations) were not fully executed to completion on the realized paired dataset and are therefore unresolved for this run.

Provider/model call budget discrepancy: planned maximum_model_calls=180 vs model_calls_used=92 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count=85); the manifest records short‑circuiting, guarded early exits, and failed calls that explain the discrepancy; these operational dynamics are logged but reduce the naïve episode→call mapping.
Construct validity: the supported/unsupported labels derive from emulator ground truth and may not capture all evidence modalities or operational complexities present in production NetOps systems.
